finding: P2O-001 — the benchmark 1% low and 0.1% low measured the FASTEST frames
mechanism: summarizeFrames sorted frame times ascending then took percentile(0.01)/percentile(0.001). On an ascending array those are the smallest frame times, i.e. the fastest frames. Converted to FPS they were published as "1% low" and "0.1% low".
sample: 100 frames at 120 fps (8.333 ms), N of them stalled to 100 ms (10 fps)

directionCheck.note: 1000-frame runs so the slowest-1% slice has 10 frames and its composition can change. More stutter must read worse.
directionCheck.retiredVerdict: unchanged at 120.00 fps — blind to stutter

note: The stalledFrames:0 row shows retiredExceedsAvg false; at N=0 the two statistics are the same number and any difference is float noise. Rows N>=1 are the demonstration.
